module: First steps and a safe learning workspace
title: Two working modes: entering data or changing the application
goal: Choose a mode for a task and distinguish user settings, records and configuration changes.

prerequisites.text: Your own empty training infobase from the previous lesson.
Understand the difference between platform, configuration and data.

sections.title: Mode describes work; role describes permissions
paragraphs: 1C:Enterprise mode runs an application. Users open lists, enter records, build reports and perform permitted operations. Designer supports development and administration: metadata, modules, forms and maintenance operations. Being able to open Designer does not establish that every change is safe. Access, competence and agreed scope are different questions.

A role determines permitted application operations. A form may hide a button for convenience, but a hidden button alone does not prove access control. Training edition omits some authentication mechanisms. We can study least privilege, while full sign-in and user-separation checks require an environment that actually supports them.

Distinguish modes by the task: change how the application is built, or work with its data. Adding a new kind of customer information belongs in Designer. Entering a particular customer into an existing catalog belongs in Enterprise mode. Do not select a more powerful mode merely because a familiar button is missing: first establish whether the required object exists at all.

sections.title: Define a field or fill in a field
paragraphs: Creating an attribute changes application structure; filling an existing field changes a record. Here, correctly separating the tasks is enough.

code.source:
Add a Phone attribute → Designer
Enter an invented customer phone → Enterprise mode
code.output: Different modes are selected for a data definition and a particular value.

sections.title: Three classes of change
paragraphs: Changing data means entering an invented request or fixing its description. A user setting changes a filter or column selection when the application exposes that option. Configuration changes add an attribute to the request type, change its type or introduce an event handler. The distinction follows the effect, not the number of clicks. A single Designer action may affect the structure of every record.

Suppose a consultant wants only open requests. If an existing filter supports this, a setting is enough. Storing a closure reason absent from the model may need a configuration change. Do not start by adding a field: first check whether an existing attribute already serves the purpose, how it is filled and which reports use it. This avoids unnecessary complexity.

A visible command and permission to perform an operation are different things. Hiding a button is not independent access protection: professional applications must enforce permissions where operations execute. This introductory lab changes no real account permissions and probes no third-party roles. Identify the intended operator or developer and choose the appropriate mode of your own infobase.

sections.title: Development has its own lifecycle
paragraphs: An edited working configuration and the database configuration are different states. Saving an application definition does not ensure that a running session already uses the new rule. A developer checks the change, updates the database configuration and separately verifies execution. A1 establishes this sequence; hands-on configuration starts in A4.

Before an update, preserve a recoverable copy. Changing an attribute type can affect stored values; an empty-looking form does not establish preservation. Agree on expected effects, then verify existing records, negative cases and recovery on a copy. The interactive diagram illustrates this process without performing an update.

The training edition may permit only one session. Open one mode, finish observing and close it before opening the other. A busy-infobase message does not justify deleting lock files or terminating every 1C process: someone else may have unsaved work. First check your own application window and save any changes that you actually intend to keep.

sections.title: The operator cannot see a configuration command
paragraphs: A command can be absent because of interface, configuration or permissions. Its absence authorizes no bypass.

code.source: The operator is assigned record entry, not structural changes.
code.output: Clarify the task and permissions instead of granting yourself maximum access.

rows: The wrong mode may be open.
Permission changes need a separate decision.

sections.title: Hand off a reproducible task
paragraphs: A useful developer request contains context, expected behavior, observed behavior and reproduction steps. “1C is broken” does not identify a test. “Filtering Status = New in the learning infobase also shows REQ-002 with status In progress” provides a checkable case. Include a synthetic example and state whether the problem remains after clearing other filters.

Do not send passwords, licensing details or a full production archive. Our course needs only a synthetic set, platform version, configuration name and chosen mode. When a task exceeds your authority, preserve a reproducible example and stop the change. This is a professional outcome, not a failure.

Your Nexus account and an infobase user are separate identities. Signing into Nexus gives access to course material and your local state; it does not create users in installed 1C. Opening a training application without a password does not demonstrate the security of a professional infobase. State which observations you made and which permissions remain untested.

sections.title: Check your explanation
paragraphs: I look for customer records in the Designer tree. The tree defines their type. Enter specific cards in Enterprise mode after the catalog exists.
I treat Nexus sign-in as 1C sign-in. These account contexts are independent; this lab changes neither.
I treat password-free training entry as security proof. The training edition has limitations; that observation does not replace permission tests in a suitable professional environment.

practice.title: One infobase, two different working windows
practice.task: Open your own infobase in both modes, one at a time. Make a table of task, mode and what you actually observed.
practice.environment: Your own file infobase in the official training platform; no changes to users or permissions.

steps.title: Check the selected infobase
steps.action: Select your own training entry. Read its name and, if needed, inspect its registered location using the standard edit-entry dialog; cancel without changes.
steps.why: The mode is meaningful only after choosing the correct infobase.
steps.expected: You can identify your own infobase and its directory.
steps.troubleshooting: If names match, compare locations. Do not delete or change someone else’s entries.
steps.before: You created your own empty training infobase in the previous lesson. Leave other infobases alone.

steps.title: Open the application definition
steps.action: Open Designer. If needed, select Configuration → Open configuration. Locate Catalogs and Documents in the tree; close the window without changes.
steps.why: This is where object types are defined, not where customer records are entered.
steps.expected: You recognize the configuration tree and created no customer records.
steps.troubleshooting: An application section panel indicates the other mode. Close only your own session and choose the correct launch button.
steps.before: You can identify your own infobase and its directory.

figures.caption: Your new personal infobase: the Designer tree is on the left; no application data exists yet.
figures.alt: Your new personal infobase: the Designer tree is on the left; no application data exists yet.

steps.title: Open the application
steps.action: After closing Designer, start Enterprise mode. Inspect the window title and available commands; an empty infobase can have no application sections. Do not attempt to grant yourself access.
steps.why: Application content depends on its configuration; this mode is for using it.
steps.expected: You can distinguish the empty application from the developer tree.
steps.troubleshooting: If it is busy, check your preceding session. Do not delete locks or terminate unrelated processes.
steps.before: You recognize the configuration tree and created no customer records.

figures.caption: A new empty infobase starts without application sections. This is the expected first result.
figures.alt: A new empty infobase starts without application sections. This is the expected first result.

steps.title: Explain what the observation establishes
steps.action: Write one task for each mode. Separately state: “This lab did not test professional infobase permissions.” Return to the lesson questions.
steps.why: An explanation must not stand in for a security test.
steps.expected: Two justified mode choices and an accurate limit of evidence are recorded.
steps.troubleshooting: If an example comes from another configuration, rewrite it for your own service desk. Do not identify a mode merely by window color.
steps.before: You can distinguish the empty application from the developer tree.
